prompt:
Create ONE brand-new independent game-environment concept image. Use ONLY the five attached master/style references in their assigned roles and this scene specification. No prior generated scene or other variation is an input. One full diorama, not a triptych.

STRUCTURE MUST KEEP
Use a single strict ORTHOGRAPHIC parallel camera, elevated quarter view, shared XYZ axes for the ENTIRE scene. Build on one flat square ground slab in cubic virtual space. All same-world-axis edges of the base, paving, building footings, wall tops and level roofs remain parallel, with no perspective convergence or depth-based scaling. Four ground corners extruded downward by a constant depth; corresponding top/bottom corners have the same vertical displacement. Show BOTH planar front cut faces and the entire base with comfortable blank margin below the nearest corner and above the highest roof. No curved ground, bent kerbs, bevelled corner, extra facets or lens distortion. Architecture ground footprints and player-contact walls are orthogonal to common X/Y axes; L/T/U plans and rectangular setbacks allowed, no diagonal or rotated building footprints. Roof joins, load-bearing supports and stair/landing connections must be coherent. Do not copy the cameras from the references.
Exactly two functional exits: one through each adjacent rear boundary direction, about 11 and 1 o'clock. Their positions/forms are specified below; keep both approaches, turning spaces and open-state connections continuously unobstructed. The center is a broad readable walking/combat area. Boundary walls/fences fill other gaps to prevent a third rear route. Front ground cut faces are not exits. The three buildings are compact: target tallest roofline around 6.3m and low supported rooftop items; the requested three storeys must read clearly. Every building has a credible human-scale door/shutter; decorative entrances remain closed unless assigned as an exit. On EACH building roof place purposeful functional equipment/props/architecture across approximately 40–80% of its footprint with support/connections and broad surface still visible. Roof occupancy is separate from the requested mechanical building fraction.

CURRENT SCENE
Urban district, alley at NIGHT. EXACTLY THREE buildings, with distinct roles A/B/C (do not render letters). Place A prominently along the LEFT flank, B as a slim freestanding building at rear-right, and C as a compact THREE-STOREY corner tenement at the far rear. All three are distinct structures joined only by boundary walls/fencing where needed. A: its whole ground storey is a salvaged municipal pump-and-power station, with two large drum housings, grounded support columns and a heavy rectangular load-bearing deck. On that deck is a recognizable one-storey moss-green HOME, with a door and residential windows. A broad straight external stair hugs A's courtyard-facing side, with evenly repeated treads, a real top landing flush to the home's door, and supported rails; it occupies the edge zone, not the main path. B: exceptionally slender frontage; a full-height modular mechanical service spine takes approximately 30% of its visible overall building mass, while the remaining majority is narrow habitation with a separate grounded entrance. C: three clearly separated compact storeys with three window tiers, a closed ground-floor door, a shallow stepped-back upper storey and a low parapet. Rooftops A/B/C have distinct functional arrangements: low duct/service deck, one grouped vent and battery rack, and low laundry-drying frame plus energy/ventilation modules; plan approximately half of each roof footprint as functional elements with visible support. Large lidded dumpster and a sorted low heap of thick scrap rings and sheet metal sit in the outer front-left recess. One utility pole is beside the outer foot of the house stair, outside its access and both exit passages, with one white lamp and a few chunky cables kept above walking height. Ground section: broad foundation layers, one ceramic drain and a separate power conduit leading to the pump base; no repeating exposed pipe wallpaper.
Paving: broad dry charcoal asphalt with two large flat slate repairs; no intersection or parking markings. Palette: muted moss-green upper house A, warm-gray narrow building B, desaturated ochre building C. 
Rear-left exit: open pedestrian alley between building C and building A; no overhead lintel. Rear-right exit: fully retracted sideways corrugated gate near the far right part of rear boundary. Stair is a domestic entrance to A's second floor and does not create a third map exit. Keep its access separate from the two protected passageways.

ART / REFERENCE ROLES — THIS TEST ONLY
Night, readable cool shadow masses and localized WHITE practical lamps. Lighting describes large planar forms; avoid hiding the exits or base under darkness, bloom or fog. Keep the road DRY; do not automatically add puddles. All architecture, utility pole, dumpster and scrap belong to Salvage Cyberpunk: advanced recovered machinery, adapter joints, replaced casings and purposeful repairs, with varied simple retro industrial controls and functional large mechanical forms. No green CRT. No characters, vehicles, phone booth, guardhouse, bicycles, comparison labels or unrequested extra buildings.
Render clean, broad, calm base-color planes on walls, paving and machinery. Leave most of each surface uninterrupted. On SELECTED intact areas add a few LARGE sparse brush marks and irregular flat pigment patches in nearby hues/values, with long-stroke direction following the surface. These color variations also occur on UNDAMAGED paint; they are not all rust, dirt or peeling. Restrict large repaired/damaged areas to a few believable places. Preserve material distinction and clear silhouettes without miniature dust or dense greebles.
The brush marks are flat COLOR, not physical relief. No embossed brush ridges, wavy contour tracing, broken-glass ripple texture, tiny mosaic rectangles, stippling, granular noise or global canvas pattern. Avoid painting every empty area with marks; keep quiet base-color space and a few broad tonal strokes. Ground should feel flat and matte. Show volume through grouped light/shadow, not microtexture. Do not turn the requested understated brush finish into uniformly smooth plastic or a featureless single-color fill.
Image 1, M01-01: full square diorama framing and two front cut faces ONLY. Exclude its perspective, commercial neon theme, exact buildings, props and markings.
Image 2, M02-01: two perpendicular rear blocking directions, two functional exits and clear connected center ONLY. Exclude diagram colors, fixed gate coordinates, icons, text and arrows.
Image 3, M03-10: large clean wall planes, selective material information and grouped light/shadow. Exclude source buildings, characters, UI, text, camera and street layout.
Image 4, M04-02: heavy functional mechanical masses, repaired broad painted housings, joints and structural assembly translated into environmental machinery ONLY. No character, limbs, face, humanoid robot or source photoreal surface density.
Image 5, user brush/light reference: broad quiet painted architecture surfaces with sparse large neighboring-tone brush patches, especially its cream facades; simple light/shadow masses. Apply that material treatment under the requested NIGHT lighting. Exclude source buildings, giant legs, harbor, boats, people, setting, perspective and daytime sky.
Do not add any text overlays, arrows, UI, watermarks or frames. Deliver one complete coherent landscape 4:3 diorama.
